searchText: The missing BLS tests from `v0.8.2` have been merged into `master` on `eth2.0-spec-tests`. We also fixed randomization to apply nil-mode to lists correctly. No release is cut for this change yet. We might cut an extremely minor `v0.8.3` (mainly aesthetic) a week from today as a final stable target for interop in Sept, but will discuss this on the call this Thursday. **cem_ozer** When deserializing a list of variable size objects, how can we know what is an offset and whats not? i.e. how can we get the end of the fixed sized part? (@schroedingerscode) **cem_ozer** Actually, the offset to the first element should be the end of the fixed size part 😄 **cem_ozer** For anyone having similar questions **schroedingerscode** (in reply to **cem_ozer**) Cem took one for the team asking this question, but it wasn't immediately obvious to me either. When you're that far down the recursion rabbit hole, some seemingly obvious things aren't. **schroedingerscode** So thanks for posting that and also coming back with an answer. It's much appreciated. **protolambda** Can confirm that reading the first offset is the way of determining the end of the fixed part. And then divide that by the length of an individual offset, and you get the count. Good question, but I am still hesitant in including a full blown deserialization spec, when it "should" (doubt) be clear from the serialization. Maybe a note on offsets could help.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
The missing BLS tests from `v0.8.2` have been merged into `master` on `eth2.0-spec-tests`. 
We also fixed randomization to apply nil-mode to lists correctly.
No release is cut for this change yet. We might cut an extremely minor `v0.8.3` (mainly aesthetic) a week from today as a final stable target for interop in Sept, but will discuss this on the call this Thursday.
